messages.content:
You trace the lineage of provisions of an Indian statute through amending Acts.
You are given ONE amending instruction, the OLD units of the principal Act it names (as they
read just before this amendment) and the NEW units it quotes. Decide, for each NEW unit, which
OLD unit it descends from (null if it is new matter) and where it sits.

Rules:
- Lineage follows content, not labels. A new clause (b) whose words are old clause (a)'s
  descends from old (a), even though the labels differ.
- A new unit descends from an old unit only if it carries that unit's substance forward.
- An OLD unit no NEW unit descends from is omitted by the instruction.
- If the instruction amends a different instrument (not the principal Act), set
  "out_of_scope": true and give no mappings.
- Use only the slot ids, old paths and allowed paths given. Each slot exactly once; each old
  unit at most once.
Reply in JSON only:
{"out_of_scope": false, "mappings": [{"slot": "<id>", "path": "<one of its allowed paths>",
  "old": "<old path or null>", "op_type": "insert|substitute|renumber",
  "confidence": 0.0-1.0, "rationale": "<one sentence>"}], "rationale": "<one sentence>"}
op_type: "insert" when old is null, "substitute" when the unit replaces its old unit at the
same path, "renumber" when it carries an old unit forward under a different path.

Amending Act: 33/2019, provision s15
Instruction: Section 26 of the Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Act, 2015 shall be omitted and shall be deemed to have been omitted with effect from the 23rd October, 2015.

The deterministic parser left this instruction unresolved because:
- amends another instrument ((Amendment) Act, 2015), not the principal Act

OLD units:
- s26: Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the arbitral tribunal may—
appoint one or more experts to report to it on specific issues to be determined by the arbitral tribunal, and
require a party to give the expert any relevant information or to produce, or to provide access to, any relevant documents, goods or other property for his inspection.
Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, if a party so requests or if the arbitral tribunal considers it necessary, the expert shall, after delivery of his written or oral report, participate in an oral hearing where the parties have the opportunity to put questions to him and to present expert witnesses in order to testify on the points at issue.
Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the expert shall, on the request of a party, make available to that party for examination all documents, goods or other property in the possession of the expert with which he was provided in order to prepare his report.

NEW units (slots):
- none

response: {"out_of_scope":true,"mappings":[],"rationale":"Instruction amends a different instrument, not the principal Act."}
